description: Look up IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic ratings, an awards summary and OMDb's own age rating (`rated`) from OMDb, by IMDb id (preferred, e.g. 'tt0133093') or by title (+ optional year/type). The awards summary is free text (major-award wins/nominations: Oscars, Emmys, Golden Globes, etc.), not a structured count, and covers the whole film/show, or one episode when given an episode's imdb_id, never one person. Prefer get_movie/get_tv when you have a TMDB id: they already include this. Requires OMDB_API_KEY. One of imdb_id or title is required; omitting both returns an error. A no-match lookup is not an error: it returns `{found:false, reason}`; a refusal (bad key, exhausted daily quota) is. A title lookup resolves to whichever single entry OMDb picks, reports no runner-up, and cannot be validated, so it can silently return a different work of the same name. Checked live: `title:'Halloween'` with no year returns the 1978 original (tt0077651, IMDb 7.7, RT 97%), not the 2018 film titled exactly the same (tt1502407, IMDb 6.5, RT 79%). Always read back the returned `imdb_id`/`title`/`year` to confirm which work you got, and pass `year` (and `type`) whenever you know them. When you only have a title, prefer search_movies/search_tv → get_movie/get_tv: that path matches by imdb_id and also drops an OMDb hit whose release year is more than two years from TMDB's, which this tool's title path cannot do.

imdb_id.description: IMDb title id. Takes precedence over title when both are given.

title.description: Movie/show title (used when imdb_id is absent).

type.description: Restrict a title lookup to this entry type. Checked live: without it, OMDb's title match can silently prefer one type when the same title exists as more than one, e.g. a lookup for 'Chuck' with no `type` returns the 2007 TV series, not the unrelated 2016 movie of the same name, with no signal the movie was ever in contention. Affects only a title lookup; no effect when imdb_id is given (already unambiguous).

name: get_ratings

imdb_rating.description: IMDb user score, 0-10, as a string, e.g. '6.5'. Not TMDB's `vote_average`.

metascore.description: Metacritic critic score, 0-100 scale, as a string, e.g. '67'.

rotten_tomatoes.description: Rotten Tomatoes Tomatometer — the percentage of positive critic reviews, as a string including the sign, e.g. '79%'. Not a 0-10 or 0-100 score.

title: Get IMDb/RT/Metacritic ratings
